_comment: Model catalogue v2 (schema 2), read by Android 0.7.0+ and desktop 0.6.0+. Builds before those read models.json (schema 1) and reject any other schema, so both files are kept; desktop/tests/test_shared.py checks that every schema-1 model appears here with the same id, repo and manifest_url. Lines are what a model is trained for (Sabich = everything, Jachnun = code-switching only, Shakshuka = streaming); variants are the same line on another base model. A variant is downloadable in an app only if its engine is in that app's supported engines AND its status is 'available'; other variants are listed greyed with runs_on and a card link. What the Models screens show is plain language (2026-10-25): base_label (e.g. Parakeet 0.6B v2 by NVIDIA), hardware, recommendation and runs_on; repo ids, formats and runtimes go in technical (and base_model, repo), shown only under Technical details. Variant ids are permanent (they name the folder models/<id>/); never reuse or rename one. speed and accuracy (1-5) and gradient (0-100) are estimates, the same numbers as hebrish.app/models/choose, not benchmark results; `chooser.rules` is that page's decision list. Protocol: shared/update-protocol.md.

recommended_by_platform._doc: Desktop builds 0.7.0+ read this before `recommended`. 0.7.0 shipped with Shakshuka here (D-2026-10-22-12); Daniel reversed that the same day (D-2026-10-22-18): Parakeet (Sabich) dictates better, and Shakshuka stays a choice. Android and older desktop builds read only `recommended`.

tiers.speed: 1 = slowest, 5 = fastest, each on the hardware it is meant for
tiers.accuracy: 1 = most mistakes, 5 = fewest, on English with Hebrew and tech words in it
tiers.gradient: 0 = smallest and fastest, 100 = most accurate; same numbers as hebrish.app/models/choose (Hebrish-Website data/variants.json)
tiers.note: Positions are estimates from model size and each model's own evaluations. The models have not all been scored on the same test set, so read them as a rough order, not a ranking.

lines.name: Sabich
lines.summary: The complete model: English with Hebrew words and tech vocabulary: arnona, Kubernetes, 250 shekels.

variants.name: Sabich
variants.hardware: Phone or computer, no graphics card needed; about 1.5 GB of memory
variants.technical: sherpa-onnx int8 offline transducer on the CPU, about 1.5 GB of RAM, no GPU.
variants.recommendation: The default, on a phone or a computer: Hebrew words and tech vocabulary, with text at each pause.

variants.name: Sabich-Qwen3-ASR-1.7B
variants.hardware: A computer with a graphics card (about 3 GB of video memory)
variants.technical: Desktop GPU: about 2.2 GB of VRAM for the Q8_0 GGUF, 5 GB for bf16 (CUDA, ROCm/HIP or Vulkan). Runs with llama.cpp (CUDA, HIP or Vulkan) and Hebrish/Sabich-Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-GGUF (Q8_0 + mmproj, about 2.2 GB), or bf16 in Transformers; transcribe.cpp Q4_K_M (1.32 GB) in Offline Voice Input on Android, slow on phones.
variants.recommendation: The most accurate, for a computer with a graphics card. Not in the Hebrish apps yet.
variants.runs_on: other speech software, on a computer with a graphics card. See the model page.

variants.name: Sabich-Canary-Qwen-2.5B
variants.hardware: A computer with a graphics card (about 6 GB of video memory)
variants.technical: Desktop GPU with about 6 GB of VRAM (bf16; PyTorch with CUDA or ROCm). Runs in NeMo (SALM) in PyTorch.
variants.recommendation: Best on plain English; behind Sabich-Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on Hebrew words. Not in the apps.
variants.runs_on: other speech software, on a computer with a graphics card. See the model page.

variants.name: Sabich-Parakeet-110M

variants.recommendation: For older phones and wearables: a fifth of the size and faster, with more mistakes.

variants.technical: FUTO asr4all M (56M parameters). The asr4all runtime: streaming CTC on the CPU, ONNX bundle on Hugging Face, with its punctuation model.
variants.recommendation: Tiny, for wearables: live text, writes numbers as words.
variants.runs_on: other speech apps. See the model page.

variants.hardware: Wearables and very low-end phones; about 0.2 GB of memory
variants.technical: FUTO asr4all S (28M parameters). The asr4all runtime: streaming CTC on the CPU, ONNX bundle on Hugging Face, with its punctuation model.
variants.recommendation: The smallest and fastest, for the weakest devices; writes numbers as words.
variants.runs_on: other speech apps. See the model page.

chooser._doc: Copied from hebrish.app's data/variants.json `rules` on 2026-10-21 (ids mapped: jachnun -> codeswitch) so the site's chooser and the apps' Help me choose agree. Checked in order; the first rule whose `when` matches wins; an absent key matches anything. Form values: device phone|computer|wearable; gpu none|amd|nvidia|apple; vram 4|8|12|16 (GB, rounded up to a bucket); priority speed|balanced|accuracy; live true|false. `how` names the build or runtime, `note` is an optional caveat.

rules.how: the ONNX bundle with ONNX Runtime, or Transformers remote code, on the CPU (streaming)
rules.reason: The smallest Sabich, and it streams, so text appears while you speak.

rules.how: NeMo cache-aware streaming, or the sherpa-onnx int8 and GGUF builds
rules.reason: Shakshuka is the streaming line: the words appear while you are still talking.
rules.runner_how: if you can wait a moment after you stop speaking: the Hebrish apps
rules.note: Shakshuka streams in the Hebrish desktop app (0.7.0+, Ubuntu and Windows) as an option for dictation; Sabich is the default. Not on Android yet.

rules.how: the ONNX bundle with ONNX Runtime, or Transformers remote code, on the CPU
rules.reason: At 28M parameters it is the smallest and fastest Sabich, built for wearables and very low-power boards. It writes numbers as words.

rules.how: sherpa-onnx int8 (about 137 MB) or GGUF Q8_0 (135 MB) with transcribe.cpp
rules.reason: NVIDIA's smallest Parakeet with all of Sabich's training: about a fifth of the size of Sabich, and it writes numbers in digits.
rules.runner_how: smaller still: the ONNX bundle on the CPU, numbers as words

rules.how: sherpa-onnx int8 or GGUF Q8_0 in Offline Voice Input
rules.reason: About a fifth of the size of Sabich, for older and low-end phones. Expect it to be less accurate.
rules.note: Sabich-Parakeet-110M is not in the Hebrish apps yet.

rules.how: the Hebrish app for Android (about 660 MB, downloaded once)
rules.reason: The most accurate model that runs well on a phone, and the default in the Hebrish app.
rules.runner_how: transcribe.cpp Q4_K_M GGUF in Offline Voice Input: it runs, but slowly

rules.how: the Hebrish app for Android (about 660 MB, downloaded once)
rules.reason: The default for phones: code-switching plus tech vocabulary, on the device.
rules.runner_how: if your phone is short on memory or speed

rules.how: the Hebrish app for Ubuntu or Windows (int8, on the CPU)
rules.reason: It runs on the CPU at dictation speed, so there is no need to go smaller.
rules.runner_how: sherpa-onnx int8, on older or slower CPUs

rules.how: the Hebrish app for Ubuntu or Windows (int8, on the CPU)
rules.reason: Without a GPU, Sabich is the best balance: accurate and quick on the CPU.
rules.runner_how: GGUF with llama.cpp on the CPU: it runs, but expect it to be slow

rules.how: the MLX build (Sabich v1.0; v2.1 has no MLX build yet) with parakeet-mlx on Apple silicon
rules.reason: Sabich has an MLX build for Apple silicon; there is no Hebrish app for Mac yet.
rules.runner_how: GGUF with llama.cpp's Metal backend (not tested yet)

rules.how: the Hebrish app for Ubuntu or Windows, or the F16 GGUF (v2.1) or ONNX (v1.0) in your own tools
rules.reason: Smaller and quicker than the Qwen model, and close behind it on accuracy.
rules.runner_how: bf16 in Transformers, about 5 GB of VRAM

rules.how: GGUF Q8_0 (about 2 GB) with llama.cpp: HIP or Vulkan on AMD, CUDA on NVIDIA
rules.reason: The highest accuracy, and the Q8_0 GGUF fits in 4 GB of VRAM.
rules.runner_how: the Hebrish app, on the CPU
rules.note: The bf16 weights need about 5 GB of VRAM; the Q8_0 GGUF needs about 2.2 GB.

rules.how: the Hebrish app for Ubuntu or Windows
rules.reason: With 4 GB of VRAM or less, Sabich is the quicker all-round choice.

rules.how: bf16 in Transformers (about 5 GB of VRAM; PyTorch ROCm on AMD, CUDA on NVIDIA), or GGUF with llama.cpp
rules.reason: Your GPU has room for it, so you get the highest accuracy at a good speed.
rules.runner_how: the Hebrish app, if you want dictation in every app now

rules.reason: The default: code-switching plus tech vocabulary.

addons._doc: Optional add-ons that are not speech models (B-40, B-40a). kind text_cleanup: a GGUF text model run once on a finished Transcription Mode transcript. Desktop (1.013+) runs it with `runtime` (a pinned llama.cpp CPU build of llama-server, per OS, downloaded with the model) and the top-level file; Android (B-40a) reads the `android` block (a smaller quantisation; llama.cpp is built into the APK) and ignores entries without one. Several entries since 2026-10-30 (Daniel): one has `default: true` (offered first and used until the user picks another); `experimental: true` is shown as such. Builds before multi-model support read only the entry with id s1-asr-cleanup. Licence: S1-mini by Superwhisper is Apache 2.0 plus a naming term: wherever an app names or describes it or a fine-tune of it, it is identified as "S1-mini" by "Superwhisper". desktop/hebrish/cleanup.py, android CleanupStore.kt
addons.name: S1-mini by Superwhisper
addons.licence: Apache 2.0 with the S1-mini naming term
addons.hardware: A computer, no graphics card needed; about 1.3 GB of memory while it runs
addons.technical: Qwen3-0.6B, the stock model, in Superwhisper's own GGUF build (Q4_K_M, 484 MB, the build its published accuracy was measured on), run on the processor by llama.cpp's llama-server (CPU build, 22 to 24 MB download). Greedy decoding with S1-mini's prompt and [Layers: 1,2].

addons.name: S1-ASR-Cleanup (fine-tune of S1-mini by Superwhisper)
addons.licence: Apache 2.0 with the S1-mini naming term
addons.hardware: A computer, no graphics card needed; about 1.2 GB of memory while it runs
addons.technical: Qwen3-0.6B architecture, GGUF Q8_0 (639 MB), run on the processor by llama.cpp's llama-server (CPU build, 22 to 24 MB download). Greedy decoding with S1-mini's prompt and [Layers: 1,2].
